title: Coverage after a school-based adolescent vaccination catch-up campaign: who caught up and who did not
subtitle: Register-based follow-up or school coverage survey, depending on data access
statement: A district catch-up campaign in spring 2026 offered the adolescent HPV, meningococcal ACWY and pertussis-containing vaccines to about 23,000 students in grades 7 to 9 across 41 schools after two disrupted school years. The district needs to know coverage after the campaign, which groups of students remain unvaccinated, and why consent forms did not return from some schools. Whether this can be answered from student-level register data or needs a school survey depends on a data-access decision that has not been made.
whoAffected: Students in grades 7 to 9 and their families, school nurses, schools and the district health department; students in deprived neighbourhoods and families speaking other languages at home are most likely to remain unvaccinated.
whatHurts: Students who missed doses remain unprotected against HPV-related cancers, meningococcal disease and pertussis, and next year's program cannot be targeted without knowing where the gaps are.
currentPractice: Doses given in schools are entered in the regional register; coverage is reported only as district totals, and nobody has looked at who caught up.
whyNow: Next year's program is planned in early 2027 and the campaign data are fresh; register access has been requested but not answered.
constraints: One epidemiologist two days a week until June 2027 and the program nurses during school hours; no new funding. Nothing may be collected in schools without school board approval, and no student may be identifiable in any output.
patientCenteredGoal: Every student in grades 7 to 9 who wants the adolescent vaccines can get them, and next year's effort goes to the schools and families the campaign did not reach.
summary: Problem framed; the design is left unresolved between a register-based follow-up and a school coverage survey until data access is known.
